## Critique
- claim-1: The cited excerpt supports only the ambient Schur basis of \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\). It does not establish the definition or graded pieces of \(J\), the Pieri formulas, or any fifteen-case matrix certificate.
- claim-2: The four displayed identities follow conditionally from the stated Pieri relations. The assertions about \(A_k\) also require the explicit unimodular changes of basis
  \[
  [h_2,h_1^2]_{(s_{(2)},s_{(1,1)})}
  =\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad
  [h_3,h_2h_1,h_1^3]_{(s_{(3)},s_{(2,1)},s_{(1,1,1)})}
  =\begin{pmatrix}1&1&1\\0&1&2\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix},
  \]
  both of determinant \(1\). Even with these additions, claim-2 establishes only the preliminary degree enumeration and row dependencies, not the required fifteen cases.
- claim-3: This correctly identifies the decisive gap. Without equation (4), its fifteen parameter cases, column orders, and full matrices, the products \(\mathcal C R_{\mathrm{selected}}=R_{\mathrm{full}}\) are underdetermined. Thus the named certificate is not established by the supplied material.

## Repair certificates
- [source-refresh] Supply the exact equation/table labeled (4) from `research-attempt-research-plan-task-68-1`, including all fifteen case conditions, every available-column order, the selected-row convention, and each intended \(R_{\mathrm{full}}\).

## Required revisions
- Define all named Schur classes and declare unavailable slots and their associated rows to be zero or omitted consistently.
- Include the two unimodular matrices above and their determinants.
- After restoring (4), derive each \(R_{\mathrm{selected}}\) independently from Pieri coordinates; then display an integral \(\mathcal C\), its dimensions, and the entrywise literal product for each of the fifteen cases.
- Conclude only whether this certificate is established; make no parent-theorem claim.
